02 — About

Point of view.

"I don't just train models.I question what the data is actually telling us."

DATA× HUMAN BEHAVIOUR× AI× PRODUCT

I'm completing my MSc in Data Science and Analytics at the University of Leeds, building on a B.Tech in Information Technology. My work sits at the intersection of machine learning, statistical rigour and product thinking — I'm as interested in why a model works as in whether it does, and in what a result actually means for the person who has to act on it.

That shows up as a habit: engineer interpretable features before reaching for complexity, validate honestly enough to trust the result, and communicate findings so a non-technical stakeholder can act on them. It's carried me from movement-kinematics research to customer analytics to a computer-vision hackathon build — different data, same discipline.

Currently, I'm exploring agentic AI by building an intelligent Personal Assistant designed to coordinate tasks, analyse information, support decision-making and automate useful workflows.

03 — Work

01 MSc Dissertation

Machine Learning
× Human Movement

Participant-independent decoding of visual-feedback information from reach-to-grasp kinematics.

2,600+
Trials analysed
23
Participants
6
ML / DL architectures
64.2%
Best accuracy
Key Takeaway

Logistic Regression on engineered kinematic features outperformed Random Forest and four deep sequence architectures (TCN, 1D-CNN, LSTM, GRU) — 64.2% participant-independent accuracy, confirmed above chance via permutation testing across 2,600+ trials and 23 participants.

Pythonscikit-learnTensorFlow/KerasR
Logistic Regression (best model)64.2%

Random Forest and all four deep sequence models (TCN, 1D-CNN, LSTM, GRU) scored lower under the same participant-independent validation.

03 Business Analytics · 2026

ICO Fundraising
Prediction

Modelled Initial Coin Offering outcomes from digital-presence, compliance and geographic signals.

Key Takeaway

For fundraising data this sparse and inconsistently reported, disciplined missing-data imputation and explicit leakage/class-imbalance controls mattered more to a trustworthy result than model choice.

PythonImputationClassification
Structured missing-data imputationExplicit leakage control
